raw_response:
I am 45 years old, been farming my land in Quzhou since I was a little boy helping my father. I only finished primary school, but I know every corner of my 3.5 mu. I have 2.5 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 1 mu I keep for cotton. My family has 4 mouths to feed, so every yuan I spend on inputs matters.

For wheat this winter on my 2.5 mu: I will rotary till the field first, then plant improved wheat seed at about 30 jin per mu. Before planting I will spread 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer. When the wheat reaches jointing stage in spring, I will top-dress with about 40 jin of urea per mu. I learned this from my father and from watching my neighbor Lao Wang — if you skip the top dressing, the wheat turns yellow and the heads come out small. I will irrigate 3 times: once in winter if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Pumping water from the well costs diesel, so I do not water for nothing, but jointing is the time you must water or you lose the harvest. I will spray twice — herbicide right after planting, and once for bugs around heading time. I expect 500 jin per mu this year, which is a bit better than the 480 jin I got last year.

For maize this summer on the same 2.5 mu: Right after I cut the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid maize straight into the wheat stubble without tilling. Everyone does this now — it saves time and diesel, and the leftover stalks keep moisture in the ground. I will buy new hybrid seed every year, about 5 jin per mu. I will put compound fertilizer down at planting, then spread urea when the maize is knee-high. I will irrigate twice, at big trumpet stage and at filling. Summer rain sometimes helps, but you cannot count on it. I will spray herbicide at planting and once for corn borers later. I expect about 550 jin per mu, same as last year if the weather holds.

For cotton on my 1 mu: I will rotary till in spring and plant improved cotton seed at about 6 jin per mu. I will put down compound fertilizer and some urea as base. Cotton needs more watching than grain — I will spray 4 times for aphids, mites, and bollworms, and irrigate 3 times. Cotton prices have been steady, so I keep this 1 mu even though it is more work. I expect about 280 jin of seed cotton per mu.

I spend carefully because 3.5 mu is not much land. I always watch what my neighbors do. If Lao Wang and the others are using a new seed and their fields look good, I will try it too, but I stick to what I know unless I see it work with my own eyes. I would rather put a bit too much fertilizer than too little — a bad harvest is a disaster for my family, but wasting some fertilizer is just money I could have saved.
